caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1250 of 2002
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury Md Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record --For the Petitioners. 	
Nurul Islam, Advocate-on-Record -For Respondent No. 1 	
Not represented-Respondent Nos. 2-17.
parties:
Abdus Sattar (Md) and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Alimon Bibi and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order, June 10, 2002, of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 728 of 2001 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the order of November 8, 2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, in charge, 1st Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1999. 

 2. Facts, in short, are that respondent No. 1 filed 3 suits in respect of the self-same subject matter. The petitioners herein also filed one suit in respect of subject matter of suits of the respondent No. 1 All the suits were heard analogously by the Court of Subordinate Judge and the said Court by the judgment and decree of February 8, 1995 dismissed the suits filed by the respondent No. 1 and decreed the suit filed by the petitioners herein. Respondent No. 1 preferred appeals. The appeals were heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka analogously and by the judgment and decree of March 25, 1999 dismissed the appeals filed against the judgment and decree passed in the respondent No. 1's suits and allowed the appeal filed against the judgment and decree passed in the suit of the petitioners herein and dismissed the suit filed by them. Thereupon the respondent No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1999 seeking review of the judgment and decree passed in the appeals filed against the judgment and decree dismissing his suits. The Miscellaneous Case was fixed for hearing on November 8, 2000. On that date on the ground of illness of the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 an application was filed seeking adjournment. The learned Additional District Judge upon rejecting the application seeking adjournment dismissed the Miscellaneous Case for default. As against the said order of the learned Additional District Judge, respondent No. 1 moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division upon observing.... "the application for adjournment was made not on any ground other than the ailment of the learned Advocate I have noticed from the order sheet of the case that on each of the previous occasions, the petitioner appeared and took proper steps in the case. The learned Additional District Judge was absolutely unjustified in rejecting the prayer for time in failing to appreciate that the learned Advocates are the officers of the Court and the Bar and the Bench are complementary to each other and that the learned Advocates are integral part of the Court. Therefore, they deserve some privilege from the Courts in respect of adjournment of any case on their personal ground" made the Rule absolute and set aside the order of dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case and further directed the learned Additional District Judge to "dispose of the Miscellaneous Case within 60 days from the date of receipt of the order without fail." 

 3. Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that one Miscellaneous Case has been filed against the judgment and decree in 3 appeals and the same being not maintainable the learned Additional District Judge did not commit any error in dismissing the said Miscellaneous Case with the observation that the Miscellaneous Case so filed was not maintainable and, as such, the High Court Division was in error in setting aside the order of the learned Additional District Judge without considering the fact that Miscellaneous Case so filed was not maintainable. The learned Counsel also submits that application upon which Miscellaneous Case has been registered does not disclose any ground for review of the judgment dismissing the 3 appeals filed by the plaintiff respondent No. 1 and, as such, the High Court Division was in error in not considering the said aspect of the Miscellaneous Case and that also in not considering the fact that the Miscellaneous Case has been filed only to harass the petitioner herein. The submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioners as to maintainability of the Miscellaneous Case are the matter for consideration by the Court before which the Miscellaneous Case has been filed. In the instant case the only consideration whether the Court was justified in dismissing the Miscellaneous Case in spite of seeking adjournment on the ground of illness of respondent No. 1's learned Advocate. The High Court Division on perusal of the record was of the view that the respondent No. 1, as the petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case, was diligently prosecuting the Miscellaneous Case and that almost on the previous all dates he took steps for hearing of the Miscellaneous Case and that only on one date ie, November 8, 2000, an application was filed seeking adjournment of hearing of the Miscellaneous Case on the ground of illness of the learned Advocate. The learned Counsel for the petitioners failed to point out any infirmity in the findings of the High Court Division upon making which said Division set aside the order dismissing the Miscellaneous Case for default.
